title.en: 1799: Cao Zhenxiu chooses her exemplary women
title.zh: 1799年：曹贞秀选择她心中的杰出女性

location.label: China: country reference point; commission location unestablished

labelI18n.en: China: country reference point; commission location unestablished
labelI18n.zh: 中国：国家层面的参考点；委绘地点未定

summary.en:
Who deserves a place in an album of exemplary women? In 1799, Cao Zhenxiu answered by writing sixteen poems and asking Gai Qi to paint their subjects. Her selection brought scholars, artists and warriors into a genre often associated with dutiful daughters and faithful widows. Choosing whom to remember was itself part of the work.

The album joins two kinds of authorship: Cao’s words and Gai’s brush. The painter was still a young man, already admired for refreshing familiar figure-painting themes. His thin lines and light washes make small pages reward close attention. A garden rock, a blade of grass or a figure’s surroundings becomes an opportunity to vary ink and texture.

The Ban Zhao leaf connects a Han historian with the Qing woman who chose to celebrate her. Read it beside Ban Zhao’s biography: one tells of scholarship and education, the other shows how a later poet and painter made learned women into models for their own time.
summary.zh:
谁值得进入一册描绘杰出女性的画册？1799年，曹贞秀以十六首诗作出回答，并请改琦为诗中人物配画。她把学者、艺术家与女将纳入这个常以孝女、节妇为典范的题材。选择纪念谁，本身就是创作的一部分。

这本画册结合了两种作者身份：曹贞秀写诗，改琦作画。改琦当时尚年轻，已因赋予传统人物画新意而受到赏识。纤细的线条与轻淡的墨色，让小幅画页值得反复细看。园石、草叶以及人物所处的环境，都成为变化笔墨与质感的机会。

其中的班昭图把汉代女史家与清代选择表彰她的女作者联系起来。不妨与班昭生平并读：一篇讲述史学和教育活动，另一篇展示后来的诗人与画家如何让有学识的女性成为自己时代的典范。

sources.title: Famous Women, 2016.362a–t
sources.evidenceNote: Dated album, sixteen poems, Cao’s commission and the variety of ink textures.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 支持画册署年、十六首诗、曹氏委绘及笔墨质感。

title.en: Chuquibamba stars within an imperial tunic
title.zh: 帝国束腰衫中的丘基班巴星纹

location.label: Southern Peru: regional reference; workshop unknown

labelI18n.en: Southern Peru: regional reference; workshop unknown
labelI18n.zh: 秘鲁南部：区域参考点；工坊未知

summary.en:
Look inside the eight-pointed stars. Their contrasting square centers help distinguish this tunic from classic Inca designs, in which such stars are usually a single color. The Met now credits the garment to a Chuquibamba artist. That change restores local makers to an object once classified chiefly through the empire that ruled their region.

Chuquibamba weaving traditions preceded Inca expansion and continued after incorporation. The garment combines local pattern choices with proportions associated with imperial tunics. Its regular grid makes the difference easy to miss: order does not mean every workshop followed exactly the same design.

A study of another tunic, excavated at Caleta Vitor in northern Chile, asks how local expertise entered imperial production. Its authors trace decisions in weaving technique as well as visible ornament, arguing that provincial makers helped transform state conventions. This comparison offers a question to bring back to the star-patterned cloth: which choices belonged to an imperial standard, and which remained in the weaver’s hands? Beside the atlas’s checkerboard Inka tunic, this garment makes variation within the empire visible.
summary.zh:
仔细看八角星的内部。星心中颜色不同的方块，使这件衣服有别于经典印加样式中通常单色的星纹。大都会艺术博物馆如今把它归于丘基班巴织工。这一归属变化，让曾主要以统治当地的帝国来分类的文物，重新显出地方制作者的存在。

丘基班巴纺织传统早于印加扩张，并在当地纳入帝国后继续发展。此衣把本地纹样与帝国束腰衫常见的比例结合起来。规整网格容易使人忽略这些差异：整齐有序，并不意味着所有工坊都遵循完全相同的设计。

对智利北部卡莱塔维托尔出土的另一件织衣，研究者追问地方技艺如何进入帝国生产。他们不仅分析可见纹饰，也追踪编织技术中的选择，提出地方制作者参与改变了国家规范。这一比较让我们带着问题重看星纹织物：哪些选择属于帝国标准，哪些仍掌握在织工手中？与地图集中的棋盘格印加织衣并看，这件衣服让帝国内部的差异变得可见。

dateNote.en: The museum dates this garment to 1460–1540, a range spanning the Spanish invasion of the Inca empire.
dateNote.zh: 博物馆将此衣断代为1460—1540年，时间范围跨越西班牙入侵印加帝国的年代。

sources.evidenceNoteZh: 支持文物断代、现行丘基班巴归属、星心图案与采用的印加比例。

title.en: A terracotta woman in Majapahit’s houses
title.zh: 满者伯夷住宅中的陶塑女子

location.label: Trowulan: architectural context, not a documented findspot

labelI18n.en: Trowulan: architectural context, not a documented findspot
labelI18n.zh: 特罗武兰：建筑背景，并非有记录的出土地

summary.en:
A woman leans her head on her right hand, her elbow supported by a rocky form. This small terracotta sculpture was made as a column surround. It brings Majapahit into view at the scale of a building’s decorated surfaces rather than a king’s conquests.

The Met relates such ornaments to the open, pavilion-like houses of the capital near Trowulan. Clay sculpture could enhance and protect columns, while ornamental tiles enlivened roofs. The woman’s clothing and hairstyle belong to Majapahit fashion. She may once have appeared in a larger sequence of scenes, although the story has not been identified.

Archaeology at Trowulan supplies the wider material setting. Indonesia’s heritage submission inventories clay water containers, money boxes, molds, roof tiles and pipes alongside sculpture. These finds place modeled figures within a city of households and workshops, not just temples. A pot and a decorated column served different purposes, but both depended on shaping clay into useful forms. Looking from this figure to the city’s domestic objects shifts attention toward the makers and residents who gave a royal capital its everyday texture.
summary.zh:
一位女子以右手托头，肘部支在岩石造型上。这件小型陶塑原是柱饰。它把满者伯夷带到眼前，尺度不再是国王的征服，而是建筑表面的装饰。

大都会艺术博物馆把这类构件与特罗武兰附近都城中开放的亭阁式住宅联系起来。陶塑可以装饰并保护柱子，装饰瓦则为屋顶增添变化。女子的服装与发式属于满者伯夷时代。她可能曾处在一组连续场景中，但具体故事尚未确定。

特罗武兰考古提供了更广阔的物质背景。印度尼西亚的遗产申报材料把陶制盛水器、储钱罐、模具、屋瓦和水管，与雕塑一并列入遗物清单。这些发现把人物陶塑放回由家庭和工坊组成的城市，而不只是寺庙的世界。陶罐与装饰柱用途不同，却都依靠把泥土塑成可用器物的技艺。从这位女子看到城市里的日用器物，我们的注意力也转向了制作者和居民：正是他们赋予王都日常生活的具体面貌。

dateNote.en: The museum dates the object to the fourteenth–fifteenth century, shown here as approximately 1300–1500.
dateNote.zh: 博物馆将此物断代为十四至十五世纪，此处约以1300—1500年表示。
